# A conservative complete conditional integer transfer

Prepared for Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.
Apache-2.0. This composition uses Jose Manuel's physical root, support,
Fourier, ring/chirp and Gaussian constructions; Tekalign's encoded CRT
conversion; the original integer-assembly and analytic sources; and the
credited pooled supplier lineage. Their source-relative premises remain
explicit. The new result is the source-specific composition and complete
cost/error comparison, not authorship of those components.

## Statement and proof boundary

Under the completed physical and analytic contracts specified below, the
pooled supplier admits a fixed finite-tape integer multiplication construction
with exact output and

```
T(n) = O(n (log n)^(1-1/580)),
space O(n)+F_q,
kappa = 1/580 = 0.0017241379310344827586... .
```

This is a conditional all-parameter composition, separate from the exact
finite release and the more aggressive legacy arithmetic candidate
`0.001727989140903569`. The conservative value includes the physical root's
actual stopping rule, both support-routing directions, the full Fourier and
Gaussian calls, three CRT conversions, normalization, integer recovery,
all child-return copies, restoration and fixed compiled inventories.

The required contracts are the pooled arbitrary-input native/common-cover
identities and whole-call hosting; the retained completed BIT/ordinary,
Compact and fixed-tape primitives; the source-relative physical root and
Gaussian refinement/locality/rounding arguments; and the stated analytic
Gaussian and prime theorems. These are mathematical premises, not conclusions
of a bounded replay. The construction does not use a rounded recursive C
child. Exact children run on one guarded grid; truncation occurs only at
the complete normalized interfaces prescribed by their source.

`OUTER-PINS.json` freezes exact proof and constructor references. It is not
an executable export of every transitive Gaussian source. PR3935 is pinned
at `f687fa171ef760fa98a4be1289717b47dd4ee0b3`; canonical references are pinned
at `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`. The source-specific global
binding and its physical proof are in `physical_global_bridge.py` and
`PHYSICAL-GLOBAL.md` (with the local refinement in `PHYSICAL-BRIDGE.md`).
The constructor/cohort comparison and exact margins
are separated in `OUTER-DOMAIN.md`; exact normalization/error controls are
in `OUTER-CHECK.md`. No complete production-prime payload, end-to-end
Gaussian integer program, human review or formal-kernel theorem is claimed.

## 1. The physical layer rate actually used

Retain PR3599's completed ordinary backend and its exact encoded coupling
`1/577`; no B2 backend is needed for this theorem. Put

```
tau = 332353/332929,
sigma_star = 0.99826995,
alpha_layer = 0.99827,
theta_stop = 1/1000000.
```

The pooled complete moment is less than one at `1-C`, where
`C=0.001730980255989036959962`. Since every child ratio is strictly below
one and `sigma_star>1-C`, it is also less than one at `sigma_star`.
Moreover `tau<sigma_star<alpha_layer`. The retained stopped-tree proof
therefore applies with its original inequality direction. Its internal
exponent is `sigma_star-theta_stop*(sigma_star-tau)` and its leaf exponent
is `sigma_star+theta_stop*(1-sigma_star)`. Both are strictly below
`alpha_layer`; the root reservation exponent is still `.998`.

Use the actual selected width `g` as the root dimension, spacing
`K=floor(g^(1/500))`, and the encoded stop `e^1000000<g`. Bind the actual
pooled provider selector, owner charts, idle suffixes, translations and
cover correction. The positive children and completed restoration have
exactly the full-replay histogram. The enlarged constant row divisor,
private bank, parent parking and dyadic guard are charged by that binding's
proof; they do not alter `tau`, the stopping power or the selected support
cap `g<=floor(p^.997)`.

The resulting source-relative root contract is
`O(V g^alpha_layer log p)` on the retained actual-record domain. PR3627's
support wrapper supplies those records, preserves complete spectators and
pays exposure and inverse exposure. Its exposed complete record field supplies
the root's long-record lower bound uniformly; the fixed long-record constants
in PHYSICAL-GLOBAL are independent of the radix digit width `b` introduced
below. Its literal fallback lifts the grid before the one-bit calls and
truncates once. The complete support cost is

```
O(V [g^alpha_layer log p + (g+1)^tau (log p)^(1+tau)]).
```

PR3640's complete synthetic Fourier schedule uses these support calls in
their natural coordinate frame. It keeps one grid of precision `P=p+A`,
so all intermediate normalized H returns are exact on that grid. Its
polynomial diagonals, endpoint bit reversal, input/output conversions and
final truncation are retained. For the shape below, its complete exponent is

```
Phi = 1-(997/1000)(1-alpha_layer) = 0.99827519.
```

The full-support router has exponent
`beta=41544341/41616125<Phi`. Its extra logarithm is paid by this strict
gap. This is the arbitrary-support route; the older exact-K transposition
invoice would give a different, insufficient bound.

## 2. One explicit integer input family

Let both integers have at most `n` bits, with leading zeros permitted.
For a sufficiently large fixed cutoff define

```
b=ceil(log2 n), p=6b,
T = the least power of two with T>=4n/b,
N=log2 T,
D=floor(p^(997/1000)), d=D+1,
ell=ceil(N/D), r=2^ell,
alpha_G=floor(p^(1/1000)), u=alpha_G^2.
```

Eventually `D>=2`, `D<N`, `ell>=2` and `T<2^b`, while
`4n/b<=T<8n/b`. Choose exactly `N-D(ell-1)` of the D target lengths to
be `r`, the remainder `r/2`, and put a long axis last. Their product is
exactly T. The actual TensorPlan parameters are `axes=D-1`,
`dimensions=D` and `d=D+1`; these names must not be interchanged.

For each target length t choose a distinct odd prime in

```
((1-1/(2d))*t, (1-1/(4d))*t).
```

The required multiplicity is at most D for each of the two target sizes.
Baker--Harman--Pintz Theorem 1 gives a prime in each sufficiently large
interval `[x-x^(21/40),x]`. As in the retained rad20 prime argument, pack
at least D disjoint such intervals inside each required interval. The
sufficient comparison `12d^2<t^(19/40)` holds eventually because
`log2 t=Theta(p^.003)` while `log d=O(log p)`. Leave endpoint room to keep
both inequalities strict. Thus the primes exist, are pairwise distinct,
and are coprime. The two size intervals are disjoint. Deterministic trial
division over the candidates costs at most
`O(D r^(3/2) poly(p))=2^o(p)=n^o(1)`; no prime advice is supplied.
The primary theorem is [Baker, Harman and Pintz, The Difference Between
Consecutive Primes, II, Theorem 1](https://www.cs.umd.edu/~gasarch/BLOGPAPERS/BakerHarmanPintz.pdf).

Put `S=product_i s_i`. Strict Bernoulli gives `T/2<S<T`. Each ratio
`rho_i=t_i/s_i` satisfies precisely

```
1/(4d) < rho_i-1 < 1/(2d-1).
```

Write each integer in base `Q=2^b`, using `q=ceil(n/b)` digits. The
polynomial product has degree at most `2q-2<2n/b<=T/2<S`, so cyclic
convolution modulo S does not wrap its nonzero coefficients. Every
coefficient is nonnegative and less than `q 2^(2b)<=2^(3b)`.

These choices give the exact asymptotic shape

```
D=Theta(p^.997), u=Theta(p^.002), ell=Theta(p^.003),
N=Theta(p), A=N-ell=Theta(p), p-A=Omega(p), Tp=Theta(n).
```

The Gaussian production requirements hold eventually: `u>=ceil(log2(8p))`,
`ud<=p`, `d>4w+2` for `w=ceil(sqrt(16p/u))+2`,
`L=2^ceil(log2(p^8))>=64dH` for `H=4096p^3`, and
`s_i>2(L+2H+2w)`. The target lengths have more than one complete L tile.
All descriptors have O(p) bits. The required source windows, period margins
and signed origins are those computed by the original-axis producer; no
unverified arbitrary coefficient page is accepted instead.

All eventual conditions are fixed before numerical input. They can be
tested by encoded integer arithmetic, including the final error gate below.
Use schoolbook multiplication if a finite-size admission fails. Each
condition eventually holds; this branch therefore covers only a fixed
bounded range of n and fits the final bound after enlarging its constant.

## 3. Complete interfaces and normalization

Write `F_-` and `F_+` for the tensor Fourier maps on the prime box, both
normalized by `1/S`. Let `R_i x(j)=x(t_i j mod s_i)` and `R=tensor_i R_i`.
The actual Gaussian endpoint is `A_-=R F_-`; conjugating its input and
output gives `A_+=R F_+`. Since `F_+ R=R^-1 F_+`,

```
A_+(A_-x * A_-y) = (x cyclic-convolve y)/S^2.
```

Here `*` is coordinatewise multiplication. Omitting R from either source
contract, treating two normalized maps as unscaled inverses, or retaining
only one factor S would change the result.

Initially scale each radix digit by `2^(-b-2)`, producing p-grid values
of modulus less than 1/4. Pad through S coefficients. Execute two complete
forward CRT conversions to natural prime-box order, then two completed
Gaussian calls. Copy and consume each protected output before reusing its
owner. Multiply corresponding returned Gaussian values exactly with four
signed integer word products, then truncate each component toward zero to
the p grid. Execute the opposite Gaussian call on that complete packet.

Every Gaussian packet uses signed least-significant-bit-first components of
width `p+2`, real before imaginary. The CRT conversion treats these as
opaque complete records of width `2(p+2)`. It preserves the complete rows
and performs its actual padding, global field permutation, triangular shifts
and cropping. It checks every discarded padding bit. There are three full
CRT conversions in total, including the final inverse below.

The synthetic Fourier maps used inside the chirp both normalize by their
polynomial-address volume M and compose to `I/M`. PR3763's completed chirp
already restores its required factors. The Gaussian theorem then supplies
`R F_s` with its exact global scale `2^gamma`. We neither add nor delete a
second normalization at these internal interfaces.

## 4. A complete error and recovery budget

Let `h=2^-p`, `M=T/r=2^A`, and

```
gamma=D(2u+ceil(log2(32p))+1),
H_err=Dp^2+32+2D.
```

PR3935 gives each completed Gaussian call, on any admitted half-disk input,
error below

```
E=2^gamma (Dp^2+4sqrt(2)M+22+2D) h
 < 2^gamma T H_err h.
```

This includes coefficient generation, expansion, the complete chirp,
principal-core compression, all local rounding, exact `2^gamma` restoration
and final width reduction. We assume the source's analytic locality and
conditioning estimates at their stated production domain. Its reduced
p48 fixture is not evidence that this asymptotic domain was executed.

Apply the additional encoded gate

```
b >= gamma+ceil(log2 H_err)+9.                         (1)
```

It holds eventually since `gamma=O(p^.999+p^.997 log p)=o(p)`.
It also implies the source guard
`p>=gamma+A+ceil(log2 H_err)+8`. Thus returned values remain in the
required disk and the retained Gaussian narrowing is valid.

For the first two exact transforms the norm is at most 1/4. Their computed
values have norm at most `1/4+E`, eventually below .26. The product's
componentwise p-grid truncation changes its Gaussian value by less than
`2h`. Its error from the product of exact transforms is at most
`E/2+E^2+2h<=E+2h`. Its norm is below `.26^2<1/2`, so the third Gaussian
call is admissible. The exact normalized map is a contraction; the complete
three-call result therefore has error below `2E+2h` from the desired
scaled cyclic convolution.

Now multiply each numerator exactly by `S^2`, restore the scale
`2^(2b+4)`, and round the real component to its unique nearest integer.
The resulting coefficient error is strictly less than

```
S^2 2^(2b+4) (2E+2h)
 < 64 H_err 2^(gamma-b)
 <= 1/8                                                (by (1)).
```

This uses `S<T<2^b` and `p=6b`. No tie occurs. The exact target is a
nonnegative integer, so the recovered real coefficient is exact; the
imaginary component rounds to zero. The exact products/shifts temporarily
use O(p)-bit signed words. Do not reinterpret those widened words as
`p+2`-bit components.

Write each recovered real coefficient in `3b+1` signed bits. Execute the
inverse CRT converter with its explicit `record_bits=3b+1` override; its
default Gaussian record width would be incorrect. It returns ordinary
coefficient order. Process that stream with base-Q carries:

```
k_0=0,
digit_j=(c_j+k_j) mod Q,
k_(j+1)=floor((c_j+k_j)/Q).
```

The invariant `0<=k_j<=q(Q-1)<Q^2` and the usual partial-sum identity
give the exact radix expansion. Drain the final carry, reverse the output
bit stream once, remove only proved-zero high padding and return exactly
`2n` bits, including leading zeros. These operations are sequential scans
with O(b)-bit carries; no per-bit random-access oracle is required.

## 5. Every cost and lifetime

The changed root has only a different finite binding and constant stock;
its completed ordinary callee remains PR3599's retuned B1. The support and
Fourier schedules retain every root call and return. PR3935's Gaussian
payload terms have powers `.997` and at most `.9981`, both strictly below
`Phi=.99827519`. Its four complete gathers have power beta, with a strict
gap to Phi for their extra logarithm. Its original-axis catalogue, periodic
halo copies, source-page reuse, numerical child returns and source setup
remain charged. `poly(t_max,p)=2^o(p)` is absorbed only after the exact
caller shape above is established.

The entire caller pays:

| Operation | Complete charge |
| --- | --- |
| Three Gaussian tensor transforms | `O(Tp p^Phi log p)` |
| Two forward and one inverse CRT conversions | `O(Tp p^beta log^(1+tau)p + D Tp + T poly(p)/r_min)` plus fixed-degree setup |
| Pointwise products, exact S-scaling and recovery | `O(Sp^(8/5))`, using the retained physical Karatsuba word engine |
| Radix input/output, copies, widening, truncation, carries | `O(Tp)` plus fixed-degree metadata setup |
| Prime search and coefficient production | `2^o(p)` with the actual polynomial producer degrees |

The inverse CRT has O(p)-bit records, so the same complete invoice applies.
The scalar word charge divided by `Sp` has power `3/5`, below Phi. No
faster unimplemented short-product oracle is needed. There is a fixed number
of numerical owners, complete packets and retained source catalogues. The
four distinct compiled ordinary instances used by the complex core, support
router, Gaussian full router and CRT full router contribute four fixed
inventories and setup constants. No instance is allocated per axis, cover
element, depth or numerical input. Parent scopes are suspended during child
calls; protected results are copied and disposed before reuse. The fixed descriptor roles occupy polynomial(p) cells. The coefficient
catalogues and their per-window headers occupy `O(poly(t_max,p))=2^o(p)`
cells, which the explicit caller shape absorbs in `O(Tp)`. Complete numerical
packets and parked payloads also occupy `O(Tp)` cells. Source compilation
contributes a fixed `F_q`.

Consequently the complete time is `O(n p^Phi log p)` and space is
`O(n)+F_q`. Since

```
1-Phi = 0.00172481 > 1/580,
```

the strict positive difference absorbs the remaining fixed logarithm.
Using `p=Theta(log n)` proves the stated conditional exponent. The target
`1/580` is above the selected `0.001672660197076918`. The old physical
Fourier rate `.00172380303` does not itself reach `1/580`; the changed
complex layer supplies the additional margin. We make no measured-runtime
claim and no uniform claim as any of these fixed margins tends to zero.

restoration term. The finite all-provider release, global source binding,
bounded exact controls and constructor evidence support different parts of

The inherited universal native/hosting, physical primitive/refinement and
